attempts: {"key_idea": "A limit describes the value a function approaches as x gets close to a point, which is not always the value the function takes at that point.", "body": "Substituting the point gives the limit only when the function is defined and well behaved there. When substitution gives an undefined expression, the limit is decided by the values of the function at inputs near the point, not by the single value at the point.", "question": "In your own words, what does a limit measure that plugging in the point does not always capture?"}

output.body: Substituting the point gives the limit only when the function is defined and well behaved there. When substitution gives an undefined expression, the limit is decided by the values of the function at inputs near the point, not by the single value at the point.
output.key_idea: A limit describes the value a function approaches as x gets close to a point, which is not always the value the function takes at that point.
output.question: In your own words, what does a limit measure that plugging in the point does not always capture?
